records.source: Συγκαλεσάμενος δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δύναμιν καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ νόσους θεραπεύειν, καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἰᾶσθαι τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μηδὲν αἴρετε εἰς τὴν ὁδόν, μήτε ῥάβδον μήτε πήραν μήτε ἄρτον μήτε ἀργύριον, μήτε ἀνὰ δύο χιτῶνας ἔχειν.
records.gloss: Having called together then the Twelve he gave to them power and authority over all the demons and diseases to heal, \v 2 and he sent them to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick, \v 3 and he said to them, Nothing take for the journey, neither staff nor bag nor bread nor money, nor apiece two tunics to have.
pieces: Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over every demon, and to cure diseases.
He sent them out to announce the kingdom of God and to heal those who were ill.
He told them, "Carry nothing with you for the road: no walking stick, no traveler's bag, no bread, no money. And none of you is to have two tunics.

L.1: Then, calling the Twelve together, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them power and authority over all the demons and to heal diseases,
L.2: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick,
L.3: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Take nothing for the journey, neither staff nor bag nor bread nor money, nor [are you] to have two tunics each.

R.1: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve apostles together. He gave them power and authority, so that every demon would obey them and they could heal diseases.
R.2: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them out to tell people about the kingdom of God and to make sick people well.
R.3: He said to them, "Do not take anything with you for your trip. Do not take a walking stick, a bag, food, or money. Take only the clothes you are wearing.

decisions.choice: power and authority: the strength to act and the right to command
alternatives: two words for the same thing
decisions.reason: Luke joins the two words when the demons obey Jesus (4:36). Now Jesus shares both with the Twelve: the power to drive demons out and the right to do it in his name.

decisions.choice: over all the demons and to heal diseases: two parts of one gift
alternatives: authority over demons and over diseases, both as things to be ruled
decisions.reason: The sentence changes shape: authority "over" the demons, then an infinitive, "to heal" diseases. Demons are to be commanded; sick people are to be cured.

decisions.choice: staff, bag, two tunics: a traveler's ordinary gear
decisions.reason: A staff was a walking stick, a bag held food and supplies, and a tunic was the long shirt worn next to the skin. They are to travel with nothing spare and rely on the people who take them in. Mark 6:8-9 allows a staff and sandals; Luke and Matthew 10:10 leave out the staff, and the point in each is to travel light.

decisions.choice: money: silver coins
decisions.reason: The word means silver, and so money in general.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: his twelve apostles
decisions.reason: Readable says who "the Twelve" are; Luke calls them apostles in 6:13 and 9:10.

decisions.choice: Take only the clothes you are wearing.
alternatives: Do not take an extra tunic.
Do not have two tunics each.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the rule about tunics: no change of clothing.

records.heading: The Twelve sent out with power

records.source: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν οἰκίαν εἰσέλθητε, ἐκεῖ μένετε καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἐξέρχεσθε.
records.gloss: And into whatever house you might enter, there remain and from there go forth.
pieces: Whatever house you go into, stay there, and leave the town from there.

L.4: And into whatever house you enter, stay there, and go out from there.

R.4: When you are welcomed into a home, stay in that same house until you leave the town.

decisions.choice: stay there, and go out from there: keep the same lodging until you leave the place
alternatives: leave each house when you have preached in it
decisions.reason: They are not to move from house to house looking for better lodging (10:7). The house where they are first welcomed is their base until they move on.

decisions.choice: leave the town (B); until you leave the town (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what they go out from, as 9:5 does.

decisions.choice: When you are welcomed into a home
decisions.reason: Readable says why they would enter a house: as guests.

records.source: καὶ ὅσοι ἂν μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐξερχόμενοι ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης τὸν κονιορτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν ἀποτινάσσετε εἰς μαρτύριον ἐπ’ αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And as many as not might receive you, going forth from the city that the dust from the feet of you shake off as a testimony against them.
pieces: If any do not welcome you, then as you leave that town, shake its dust off your feet. That will be evidence against them."

L.5: And as many as do not receive you, as you go out from that town, shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony against them."

R.5: If the people of a town do not welcome you, leave that town. As you go, shake the dust of it off your feet. This will be a warning to them."

decisions.choice: shake off the dust from your feet: a sign that the town is left to answer for itself
alternatives: a way of cleaning the feet
decisions.reason: The gesture says that the messengers carry nothing of that town with them; they have done their part. Paul and Barnabas do it at Pisidian Antioch (Acts 13:51).

decisions.choice: as a testimony against them: evidence that they were warned
alternatives: a testimony to them, meant to win them over
decisions.reason: The word means a witness or evidence. With "against" it points to the time of judgment, when the town cannot say it never heard (10:10-12).

decisions.choice: city: town
decisions.reason: The word is used for any town with walls or a center, however small.

decisions.choice: evidence (B); a warning (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for what the gesture shows.

records.source: ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ διήρχοντο κατὰ τὰς κώμας εὐαγγελιζόμενοι καὶ θεραπεύοντες πανταχοῦ.
records.gloss: Going forth then they were passing through the villages proclaiming the good news and healing everywhere.
pieces: So they set out and went from village to village, bringing the good news and healing people everywhere.

L.6: And going out, they were going through the villages, proclaiming the good news and healing everywhere.

R.6: So the apostles left and went from one village to another. Everywhere they went, they told people the good news and healed the sick.

decisions.choice: proclaiming the good news: announcing God's good news
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for good news, the word Jesus uses of his own work in 4:18 and 4:43. The message is the kingdom of God (9:2).

decisions.choice: were going through: a continuing activity
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes a mission that went on from place to place.

decisions.choice: the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject.

records.source: Ἤκουσεν δὲ Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὰ γινόμενα πάντα, καὶ διηπόρει διὰ τὸ λέγεσθαι ὑπό τινων ὅτι Ἰωάννης ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν, ὑπό τινων δὲ ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐφάνη, ἄλλων δὲ ὅτι προφήτης τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη.
records.gloss: Heard now Herod the tetrarch the things being done all, and was perplexed because it was said by some that John has been raised out from [the] dead, \v 8 by some also that Elijah had appeared, by others also that a prophet one of the ancients had arisen.
pieces: Herod the tetrarch heard about everything that was taking place, and he did not know what to make of it. Some people were saying that John had been raised from the dead;
some, that Elijah had appeared; and others, that one of the prophets from long ago had risen again.

L.7: Now Herod the tetrarch heard about all the things that were happening, and he was at a loss, because it was being said by some that John had been raised from [the] dead,
L.8: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the prophets of old had risen.

R.7: Herod, the ruler of Galilee, heard about all the things that were going on. He was confused, because people were saying different things. Some said, "John the Baptist has come back from death."
R.8: Others said, "Elijah has appeared." Still others said, "One of the prophets who lived long ago has come back to life."

decisions.choice: Herod the tetrarch: Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee and Perea
decisions.reason: This is the son of Herod the Great (1:5). A tetrarch ruled part of a land under Roman authority (3:1). He had put John in prison (3:19-20).

decisions.choice: was at a loss: puzzled, unable to decide what was happening
decisions.reason: The verb describes someone who cannot find a way through a question. The reports about Jesus did not fit together.

decisions.choice: Elijah had appeared: the prophet whose return Malachi promised
decisions.reason: Elijah was taken up alive (2 Kings 2:11), and God promised to send him before the day of the LORD (Malachi 4:5). People were waiting for him to come back.

decisions.choice: three short quotations
decisions.reason: Readable lets each group speak for itself to keep the sentences short.

decisions.choice: the ruler of Galilee
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title, as at 3:19.

records.heading: Herod hears about Jesus

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης· Ἰωάννην ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα· τίς δέ ἐστιν οὗτος περὶ οὗ ἀκούω τοιαῦτα;
records.gloss: Said then Herod, John I beheaded; who however is this concerning whom I hear such things?
pieces: But Herod said, "I cut off John's head myself. Who, then, is this man I keep hearing such things about?"

L.9: But Herod said, "John I beheaded; but who is this about whom I hear such things?"

R.9: Herod said, "I had John's head cut off. So who is this man? I keep hearing about the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does."

decisions.choice: I beheaded John: I had him beheaded
decisions.reason: A ruler is said to do what he orders. The "I" is emphatic: Herod knows John is dead because he gave the order. Luke does not tell the story of John's death; Mark 6:17-29 does.

decisions.choice: who is this: the question the chapter keeps asking
decisions.reason: Herod's question is answered by the crowds (9:19), by Peter (9:20), and by the voice from the cloud (9:35).

decisions.choice: this man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "this man" for the pronoun.

decisions.choice: I had John's head cut off
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Herod gave the order.

records.source: καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And he was seeking to see him.
pieces: And he kept trying to see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.9: And he was seeking to see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.9: So Herod kept trying to see Jesus.

decisions.choice: was seeking: kept trying
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes a continuing wish. Herod finally sees Jesus at his trial (23:8).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the one Herod wanted to see.

records.source: Καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες οἱ ἀπόστολοι διηγήσαντο αὐτῷ ὅσα ἐποίησαν.
records.gloss: And having returned the apostles related to him whatever they had done.
pieces: The apostles came back and gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} an account of everything they had done.

L.10: And when the apostles returned, they told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all that they had done.

R.10: When the apostles came back, they told Jesus about everything they had done.

decisions.choice: apostles: those sent out
decisions.reason: The word means messengers sent on a task. Jesus gave the Twelve this name (6:13), and Luke uses it as they come back from being sent (9:2).

decisions.choice: told: described in full
decisions.reason: The verb means to tell a story through from start to finish.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus at the start of a new section.

records.heading: Bread for five thousand

records.source: καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ὑπεχώρησεν κατ’ ἰδίαν εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Βηθσαϊδά.
records.gloss: And having taken them he withdrew by himself into a town called Bethsaida.
pieces: He took them with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and slipped away privately to a town called Bethsaida.

L.10: And taking them along, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} withdrew by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to a town called Bethsaida.

R.10: Then Jesus took them with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they went away by themselves to a town called Bethsaida.

decisions.choice: to a town called Bethsaida: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: to a deserted place belonging to a town called Bethsaida
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts read "to a town called Bethsaida". Many others read "to a deserted place", or join the two: "to a deserted place belonging to a town called Bethsaida". Those readings may have come in from 9:12, where the disciples say they are in a deserted place. The SBLGNT follows the early manuscripts. Either way the feeding happens in open country near the town. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: by himself: privately, away from the crowds
decisions.reason: He takes the apostles with him; the phrase means they went apart from other people.

decisions.choice: Bethsaida: a fishing town at the north end of the Lake of Galilee
decisions.reason: Bethsaida lay near where the Jordan enters the lake. Philip, Andrew and Peter came from there (John 1:44).

decisions.choice: they went away by themselves
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Jesus and the apostles went apart together.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι γνόντες ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: The but crowds having known [it] followed him.
pieces: But the crowds found out and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.11: But the crowds, learning [of it], followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.11: But the crowds found out where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going, and they followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: learning of it: finding out where he had gone
decisions.reason: The verb means to come to know. The plan to be alone did not last long.

decisions.choice: where he was going
decisions.reason: Readable says what the crowds found out.

records.source: καὶ ἀποδεξάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τοὺς χρείαν ἔχοντας θεραπείας ἰᾶτο.
records.gloss: And having received them he was speaking to them concerning the kingdom of God, and those need having of healing he was healing.
pieces: He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cured those who needed to be healed.

L.11: And welcoming them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking to them about the kingdom of God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was healing those who had need of healing.

R.11: Jesus welcomed them. He talked to them about the kingdom of God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed the people who were sick.

decisions.choice: welcoming them: receiving them gladly
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive a guest. Though he had gone away to be private, Jesus welcomes the crowd.

decisions.choice: was speaking, was healing: continuing actions
alternatives: a single word and a single healing
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes teaching and healing that went on through the day (9:12).

decisions.choice: healing: care that makes well
decisions.reason: The noun can mean service or treatment; with "need" it means healing.

records.source: Ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤρξατο κλίνειν· προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δώδεκα εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἀπόλυσον τὸν ὄχλον, ἵνα πορευθέντες εἰς τὰς κύκλῳ κώμας καὶ ἀγροὺς καταλύσωσιν καὶ εὕρωσιν ἐπισιτισμόν, ὅτι ὧδε ἐν ἐρήμῳ τόπῳ ἐσμέν.
records.gloss: And the day began to decline; having come then the Twelve said to him, Dismiss the crowd, that having gone into the surrounding villages and countryside they might lodge and might find provisions, for here in a desolate place we are.
pieces: As the day was ending, the Twelve came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "Dismiss the crowd," they said. "Then they can go to the villages and farms around here and find somewhere to stay and something to eat. This is a lonely place."

L.12: Now the day began to decline; and the Twelve came and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Send the crowd away, so that, going into the surrounding villages and countryside, they may find lodging and get provisions, because here we are in a desolate place."

R.12: When the sun began to go down, the twelve apostles came to Jesus. They said, "Send the people away. They can go to the villages and farms nearby and find a place to sleep and food to eat. There is nothing out here."

decisions.choice: the day began to decline: evening was coming
decisions.reason: The verb means to bend or lean; the day was leaning toward evening, as in 24:29.

decisions.choice: find lodging: find somewhere to stay the night
decisions.reason: The verb first meant to loosen a pack animal's load; it came to mean stopping for the night.

decisions.choice: a desolate place: open country with no one living there
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the wilderness where John lived (1:80; 3:2). Near Bethsaida it means empty land with grass (Mark 6:39), not desert.

decisions.choice: There is nothing out here.
alternatives: we are in a desolate place
decisions.reason: Readable says why the place is a problem: there is no food or shelter.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν.
records.gloss: He said then to them, Give to them you to eat.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Give them something to eat yourselves."

L.13: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "You give them [something] to eat."

R.13: But Jesus answered, "You give them food to eat."

decisions.choice: you: emphatic
decisions.reason: The pronoun is not needed in the sentence, so it is stressed: the disciples themselves are to feed the crowd. Compare Elisha's command in 2 Kings 4:42-44.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οὐκ εἰσὶν ἡμῖν πλεῖον ἢ ἄρτοι πέντε καὶ ἰχθύες δύο, εἰ μήτι πορευθέντες ἡμεῖς ἀγοράσωμεν εἰς πάντα τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον βρώματα.
records.gloss: But they said, Not there are to us more than loaves five and fish two, if not having gone we should buy for all the people this food.
pieces: They answered, "We have nothing but five loaves of bread and two fish, unless we go and buy food ourselves for this whole crowd."

L.13: But they said, "We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we are to go and buy food for all these people."

R.13: They answered, "All we have is five small loaves of bread and two fish. Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to go and buy food for all these people?"

decisions.choice: unless we go and buy: a doubtful suggestion
alternatives: a firm plan to buy food
decisions.reason: The form expresses something that might be done but is hardly likely. The disciples are pointing out that they could not buy food for so many.

decisions.choice: loaves: small flat rounds of bread
decisions.reason: A loaf was a small round of bread, one person's portion at a meal.

decisions.choice: a question: Do you want us to go and buy food?
alternatives: unless we go and buy food
decisions.reason: Readable turns the doubtful "unless" into the question it implies.

records.source: ἦσαν γὰρ ὡσεὶ ἄνδρες πεντακισχίλιοι.
records.gloss: They were for about men five thousand.
pieces: There were about five thousand men there.

L.14: For there were about five thousand men.

R.14: About five thousand men were there.

decisions.choice: men: adult males
decisions.reason: The word means males, not people in general. Crowds were counted by the men; Matthew 14:21 adds that women and children were there as well.

decisions.choice: for: explaining the disciples' worry
alternatives: giving a new fact unrelated to what was said
decisions.reason: The size of the crowd explains why five loaves seemed hopeless.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Κατακλίνατε αὐτοὺς κλισίας ὡσεὶ ἀνὰ πεντήκοντα.
records.gloss: He said then to the disciples of him, Make sit down them [in] groups of about fifty.
pieces: He told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Get them to sit down in groups of fifty or so."

L.14: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Have them recline in groups of about fifty each."

R.14: Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Tell the people to sit down in groups. Put about fifty people in each group."

decisions.choice: recline: sit or lie down for a meal
decisions.reason: People reclined at a meal, leaning on one elbow; here they sit down on the grass to eat.

decisions.choice: groups of about fifty: an orderly company
decisions.reason: Moses grouped the people under leaders over fifties (Exodus 18:21). The crowd is arranged like God's people in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: followers
decisions.reason: Readable sometimes calls the disciples followers, which is what the word means.

records.source: καὶ ἐποίησαν οὕτως καὶ κατέκλιναν ἅπαντας.
records.gloss: And they did so and made sit down all.
pieces: They did this, and everyone sat down.

L.15: And they did so and had them all recline.

R.15: The followers did what Jesus said, and all the people sat down.

decisions.choice: had them recline: sat them down for a meal
decisions.reason: The same verb as 9:14.

decisions.choice: The followers ... what Jesus said
decisions.reason: Readable names who acted and whose word they followed.

records.source: λαβὼν δὲ τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ κατέκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς παραθεῖναι τῷ ὄχλῳ.
records.gloss: Having taken then the five loaves and the two fish, having looked up to the heaven he blessed them and broke [them], and he kept giving [them] to the disciples to set before the crowd.
pieces: He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven and said a blessing over them. He broke them and kept handing them to the disciples to serve to the crowd.

L.16: Then taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up to heaven, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blessed them and broke [them], and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept giving [them] to the disciples to set before the crowd.

R.16: Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish. He looked up to heaven and thanked God for the food. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the bread and the fish into pieces. He kept giving the pieces to the disciples, and they gave them to the people.

decisions.choice: blessed them: spoke the blessing over the food
alternatives: made the food holy by a word of power
decisions.reason: A Jewish meal began with a blessing that praised God for the bread. Looking up to heaven shows to whom it was spoken.

decisions.choice: kept giving: a continuing action
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures him handing out bread again and again. Luke does not say how the food was multiplied; it kept coming from his hands.

decisions.choice: took, blessed, broke, gave: the words of the Last Supper
decisions.reason: The same steps describe the Last Supper (22:19) and the meal at Emmaus (24:30).

decisions.choice: thanked God for the food
decisions.reason: Readable explains the blessing as praise and thanks to God.

records.source: καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν πάντες, καὶ ἤρθη τὸ περισσεῦσαν αὐτοῖς κλασμάτων κόφινοι δώδεκα.
records.gloss: And they ate and were satisfied all, and was taken up that having been surplus to them of fragments baskets twelve.
pieces: Everyone ate and had plenty. Then what they had left was gathered up: twelve baskets full of broken pieces.

L.17: And they ate and were all satisfied, and what was left over by them was picked up, twelve baskets of broken pieces.

R.17: Everyone ate as much as they wanted. Then the disciples picked up the pieces that were left over. They filled twelve baskets!

decisions.choice: satisfied: had all they wanted
decisions.reason: The verb is used for being well fed (6:21). Jesus' words in 6:21 come true here for a hungry crowd.

decisions.choice: baskets: hand baskets for carrying food
decisions.reason: The word is for a basket a traveler might carry. There is one for each of the Twelve.

decisions.choice: was picked up: the passive leaves the gatherers unnamed
decisions.reason: Luke does not say who gathered the pieces; the disciples, who served the food, are the natural ones to do it.

decisions.choice: the disciples
decisions.reason: Readable names who gathered the leftovers, as the context suggests.

records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν προσευχόμενον κατὰ μόνας συνῆσαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί, καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς λέγων· Τίνα με οἱ ὄχλοι λέγουσιν εἶναι;
records.gloss: And it came to pass as was he praying in solitary, were with him the disciples, and he questioned them saying, Whom me the crowds pronounce to be?
pieces: One time Jesus was praying in a quiet place, and only the disciples were with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He asked them, "Who do the people in the crowds say I am?"

L.18: And it happened, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was praying alone, the disciples were with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} questioned them, saying, "Who do the crowds say that I am?"

R.18: One day Jesus was praying away from the crowds. Only {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Jesus asked them, "Who do the people say I am?"

decisions.choice: alone: away from the crowds
alternatives: with no one at all near him
decisions.reason: Luke says in the same breath that the disciples were with him. Alone means apart from the crowds, with only the disciples near.

decisions.choice: while he was praying: Luke's turning points come in prayer
decisions.reason: Luke shows Jesus praying at his baptism (3:21), before choosing the Twelve (6:12), here, and on the mountain (9:28-29).

decisions.choice: Who do the crowds say that I am: a question about public opinion
alternatives: a question testing the disciples' own faith
decisions.reason: The first question is about what others say; the personal question follows in 9:20.

decisions.choice: in a quiet place (B); away from the crowds (R)
decisions.reason: "Alone" would contradict the disciples' presence in the same sentence.

records.heading: Peter says who Jesus is

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν, ἄλλοι δὲ ὅτι προφήτης τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη.
records.gloss: And answering they said, John the Baptist, others also Elijah, others now that a prophet one of the ancients has arisen.
pieces: They replied, "John the Baptist. Others say Elijah. Others say that one of the prophets of long ago has risen again."

L.19: And they answered and said, "John the Baptist, and others, Elijah, and others, that one of the prophets of old has risen."

R.19: They answered, "Some say that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are John the Baptist. Others say that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are Elijah. Others say that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are one of the prophets from long ago who has come back to life."

decisions.choice: the same answers Herod heard
decisions.reason: The list repeats what was said to Herod (9:7-8): the crowds see Jesus as a prophet come back from the dead.

decisions.choice: has risen: come back to life
decisions.reason: The verb can mean simply to appear, but with "one of the prophets of old" it means rising from the dead, as in 9:8.

decisions.choice: Some say that you are
decisions.reason: Readable fills out the clipped answers.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι;
records.gloss: He said then to them, You however whom me do pronounce to be?
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "But what about you? Who do you say I am?"

L.20: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "But you, who do you say that I am?"

R.20: Then Jesus asked them, "But what about you? Who do you say that I am?"

decisions.choice: but you: emphatic and set in contrast to the crowds
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first: whatever the crowds say, what do the disciples say?

decisions.choice: you: plural, the question is to all the disciples
decisions.reason: The verb and pronoun are plural; Peter answers for the group.

records.source: Πέτρος δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Τὸν χριστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Peter then answering said, The Christ of God.
pieces: Peter answered, "You are God's {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}."

L.20: And Peter answered and said, "The {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} of God."

R.20: Peter answered, "You are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the King God promised to send."

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, God's anointed King
decisions.reason: With the article it is a title: the King whom God anoints and sends, promised in the Scriptures (2:11, 26; 4:41).

decisions.choice: of God: the one God has anointed and sent
decisions.reason: The words mean the Christ who belongs to God, as "the Lord's Christ" in 2:26. Psalm 2:2 speaks of the LORD and his anointed.

decisions.choice: God's Christ (B); the King God promised to send (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Peter's short answer a full sentence and say what "of God" means.

records.source: Ὁ δὲ ἐπιτιμήσας αὐτοῖς παρήγγειλεν μηδενὶ λέγειν τοῦτο, εἰπὼν ὅτι Δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθῆναι.
records.gloss: And having strictly warned them he instructed [them] to no one to tell this, \v 22 having said, It is necessary for the Son of Man many things to suffer and to be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes and to be killed and on the third day to be raised.
pieces: He gave them strict orders not to tell this to anyone.

"The Son of Man has to suffer a great deal," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "The elders, the chief priests and the scribes will reject {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He will be put to death, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised."

L.21: But strictly warning them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered [them] to tell this to no one,
L.22: saying, "It is necessary for the Son of Man to suffer many things and to be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and to be killed, and on the third day to be raised."

R.21: Jesus gave them a firm order not to tell anyone about this.
R.22: He said, "The Son of Man must go through many sufferings. The leaders of the people, the chief priests, and the teachers of the law will reject {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but on the third day God will raise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to life."

decisions.choice: it is necessary: what must happen in God's plan
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for what God has purposed and the Scriptures foretell (2:49; 24:7, 26, 44). Jesus is not guessing; he is saying what must be.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: As in 5:24, the title points to the one in Daniel's vision who receives everlasting rule. Here it is joined, for the first time in Luke, to suffering.

decisions.choice: the elders, chief priests and scribes: the groups of the Jewish council
decisions.reason: The leading men of the people, the senior priests and the experts in the law made up the council in Jerusalem that would hand Jesus over (22:66).

decisions.choice: to be raised: God will raise him
alternatives: he will rise by his own power
decisions.reason: The passive form leaves God as the one who raises him, as Acts 2:24 says.

decisions.choice: tell this to no one: keep Peter's answer quiet for now
decisions.reason: The command follows Peter's confession. Jesus at once explains what kind of Christ he is: one who suffers before he is raised (24:26).

decisions.choice: the leaders of the people, the chief priests, and the teachers of the law
alternatives: the elders, chief priests and scribes
decisions.reason: Readable explains each group in plain words. "Scribes" (L, B) is explained as "teachers of the law" as in 5:21.

decisions.choice: God will raise him to life
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who raises, as the passive implies.

records.source: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς πάντας· Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἔρχεσθαι, ἀρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καθ’ ἡμέραν, καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.
records.gloss: He was saying then to all, If anyone desires after me to come, let him deny himself and let him take up the cross of him every day, and let him follow me.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to everyone, "Anyone who wants to come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} must say no to {{gender:themselves|himself}}, pick up {{gender:their|his}} cross every day, and keep following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.23: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to all, "If anyone wants to come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, let {{gender:them|him}} deny {{gender:themselves|himself}} and take up {{gender:their|his}} cross daily, and let {{gender:them|him}} follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.23: Then Jesus spoke to all the people. "If anyone wants to come with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{gender:they|he}} must stop living for {{gender:themselves|himself}}. {{gender:They|He}} must take up {{gender:their|his}} cross every day, ready to die, and keep following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: daily: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: "Daily" is in the earliest manuscripts but is missing from some others, perhaps to match Matthew 16:24 and Mark 8:34, which do not have it. The SBLGNT keeps it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: take up his cross: carry the cross like a man on the way to execution
decisions.reason: Rome made a man condemned to crucifixion carry his own cross to the place of death (23:26; John 19:17). The disciple is to live as one who has given up his life, and Luke's "daily" makes it a way of life.

decisions.choice: deny himself: say no to self
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for Peter's denial of Jesus (22:34, 57). The disciple is to disown his own claims and follow Jesus instead.

decisions.choice: come after me: follow as a disciple
decisions.reason: A disciple walked behind the teacher; the sentence ends with the same thought: "follow me".

decisions.choice: stop living for themselves
decisions.reason: Readable says what denying oneself means.

decisions.choice: ready to die
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of carrying a cross.

decisions.choice: they / themselves / their as the default, he / himself / his as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Anyone" means men and women, so the pronouns that refer back to it follow the gender setting.

records.heading: Taking up the cross every day

records.source: ὃς γὰρ ἂν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι, ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ, οὗτος σώσει αὐτήν.
records.gloss: Whoever for might desire the life of him to save, will lose it; whoever however might lose the life of him on account of me, he will save it.
pieces: Anyone who sets out to save {{gender:their|his}} own life will lose it. But anyone who loses {{gender:their|his}} life because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will save it.

L.24: For whoever wants to save {{gender:their|his}} life will lose it; but whoever loses {{gender:their|his}} life on account of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{gender:that person|he}} will save it.

R.24: Anyone who tries to keep {{gender:their|his}} life safe will lose it. But anyone who loses {{gender:their|his}} life for following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will save it.

decisions.choice: life: the self, the whole person and life itself
alternatives: soul as distinct from the body
decisions.reason: The word means a person's life, the self who lives it. Holding on to life now means losing life with God; giving it up for Jesus means finding it (17:33).

decisions.choice: save: keep safe from loss, and in the end save from death
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for being saved by God (7:50; 8:12). The saying plays on two levels: keeping one's life now, and being kept for eternal life.

decisions.choice: for: giving the reason for 9:23
decisions.reason: This explains why taking up the cross is worth it.

decisions.choice: for following me
decisions.reason: Readable says how a disciple loses life for Jesus' sake.

records.source: τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖται ἄνθρωπος κερδήσας τὸν κόσμον ὅλον ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἀπολέσας ἢ ζημιωθείς;
records.gloss: What for is profited a man having gained the world whole, himself now having destroyed or having suffered the loss of?
pieces: Suppose someone wins the whole world but is ruined and loses {{gender:themselves|himself}}. What has {{gender:that person|he}} gained?

L.25: For what is {{gender:a person|a man}} profited, having gained the whole world but having destroyed or forfeited {{gender:themselves|himself}}?

R.25: Suppose someone gets everything in the world, but loses {{gender:their|his}} own self and is ruined. What good is the world to {{gender:them|him}} then?

decisions.choice: destroys or forfeits himself: loses the self for good
decisions.reason: The two verbs say the same thing twice for force: the person is lost and has nothing left to show.

decisions.choice: the world: all that people can own and achieve
decisions.reason: Here the world is wealth, power and success, everything one might gain in this life.

decisions.choice: himself: the person's own self, the life of 9:24
decisions.reason: Luke has "himself" where Mark 8:36 has "his life"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: a statement, then the question
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable split the long question in two.

records.source: ὃς γὰρ ἂν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους, τοῦτον ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται, ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων.
records.gloss: Whoever for may have been ashamed of me and my words, him the Son of Man will be ashamed of, when he shall come in the glory of himself and of the Father and of the holy angels.
pieces: If anyone is ashamed of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of {{gender:that person|him}} when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own glory and the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.

L.26: For whoever is ashamed of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, of {{gender:that person|him}} the Son of Man will be ashamed when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory and [the glory] of the Father and of the holy angels.

R.26: If anyone is ashamed of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and of what I teach, the Son of Man will be ashamed of {{gender:that person|him}}. That will happen when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, with the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.

decisions.choice: be ashamed of: refuse to be known as belonging to
decisions.reason: To be ashamed of Jesus is to disown him in public. The Son of Man will in turn disown that person at the judgment (12:8-9).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man comes in glory with the angels: Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: Daniel saw one like a son of man come with the clouds and receive glory and rule. Jesus speaks of himself coming to judge.

decisions.choice: his glory and the Father's and the holy angels': one glory shared
decisions.reason: He comes in his own glory, which is also the Father's, and the angels come with him (Mark 8:38).

decisions.choice: what I teach
decisions.reason: Readable says what his words are.

records.source: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ἀληθῶς, εἰσίν τινες τῶν αὐτοῦ ἑστηκότων οἳ οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: I say now to you truthfully, there are some of those here standing who not not shall taste of death until they shall have seen the kingdom of God.
pieces: I tell you truly: among those standing here are some who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God."

L.27: But I tell you truly, there are some of those standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see the kingdom of God."

R.27: I tell you the truth, some people standing here will see the kingdom of God before they die."

decisions.choice: truly: in truth
decisions.reason: Luke has the ordinary word for "truly" here, not the Hebrew word amen (4:24). The force is the same.

decisions.choice: taste death: die
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of saying die (John 8:52; Hebrews 2:9).

decisions.choice: see the kingdom of God: see God's rule come in power
decisions.reason: What they will see is debated: the transfiguration that follows (9:28-36), Jesus' resurrection and the coming of the Spirit, or the kingdom's coming in power. Luke places the transfiguration straight after the promise.

decisions.choice: certainly not: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two negatives together for an emphatic denial.

decisions.choice: before they die
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὡσεὶ ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ καὶ παραλαβὼν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι.
records.gloss: It came to pass now after the sayings these about days eight, and having taken Peter and John and James he went up on the mountain to pray.
pieces: Some eight days after these words, Jesus went up the mountain to pray, taking Peter, John and James along.

L.28: Now it happened, about eight days after these sayings, that taking Peter and John and James, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up onto the mountain to pray.

R.28: About a week later, Jesus took Peter, John, and James and climbed a mountain to pray.

decisions.choice: about eight days: about a week
decisions.reason: Mark 9:2 and Matthew 17:1 say "after six days". Luke's "about eight days" counts the day of the sayings and the day of the climb; both mean about a week later.

decisions.choice: after these sayings: linked to the promise of 9:27
alternatives: a new story with no link
decisions.reason: Luke ties what happens on the mountain to the words just spoken, including the promise that some would see the kingdom of God.

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hill country, not named
alternatives: a mountain named in the text
decisions.reason: Luke does not name the mountain. Later tradition named Mount Tabor; others suggest Mount Hermon, nearer Caesarea Philippi.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: About a week later
alternatives: about eight days after these sayings
decisions.reason: Readable gives the idiom's meaning.

records.heading: Jesus is changed on the mountain

records.source: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ προσεύχεσθαι αὐτὸν τὸ εἶδος τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἕτερον καὶ ὁ ἱματισμὸς αὐτοῦ λευκὸς ἐξαστράπτων.
records.gloss: And it came to pass in the praying of him the appearance of the face of him [was] altered and the clothing of him white flashing.
pieces: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prayed, the look of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face was changed, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes turned white and flashed like lightning.

L.29: And it happened, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was praying, the appearance of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face [became] different, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothing [became] white, flashing [like lightning].

R.29: While Jesus was praying, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face began to look different. His clothes became bright white, flashing like lightning.

decisions.choice: flashing: gleaming like lightning
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for lightning and describes a sudden brilliant flash.

decisions.choice: the appearance of his face became different: compare Moses' shining face
decisions.reason: When Moses came down from speaking with God, the skin of his face shone (Exodus 34:29-35). Luke does not use the word "transformed" that Mark 9:2 uses, but the change is from God.

decisions.choice: as he was praying: the change comes in prayer
decisions.reason: Jesus went up to pray (9:28), and it is while he prays that his glory is seen.

decisions.choice: like lightning
decisions.reason: The verb itself suggests lightning; Balanced and Readable say so, and Literal puts the words in brackets.

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο συνελάλουν αὐτῷ, οἵτινες ἦσαν Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας, οἳ ὀφθέντες ἐν δόξῃ ἔλεγον τὴν ἔξοδον αὐτοῦ ἣν ἤμελλεν πληροῦν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ.
records.gloss: And behold men two began talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah, \v 31 who having appeared in glory were speaking of the going out of him which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.
pieces: Suddenly two men were talking with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: Moses and Elijah.
They appeared in glory and were speaking of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} departure, the exodus {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was about to complete in Jerusalem.

L.30: And look, two men were talking with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who were Moses and Elijah,
L.31: who, appearing in glory, were speaking of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} exodus, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was about to fulfill in Jerusalem.

R.30: Then two men were there talking with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were Moses and Elijah.
R.31: They appeared in heavenly glory, and they talked with Jesus about how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would soon leave this world. This would happen in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: exodus: departure, his going out of this life
decisions.reason: The word means a going out, and is used for death (2 Peter 1:15). It is also the name of Israel's going out of Egypt, led by Moses (Hebrews 11:22). With Moses present, the word suggests that Jesus will lead a new exodus through his death, resurrection and ascension in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: fulfill: bring to completion
decisions.reason: The verb means to fill up or complete. His departure is a task he will carry out, not only something that happens to him.

decisions.choice: Moses and Elijah: the Law and the Prophets
decisions.reason: Moses gave the law, and Elijah stands for the prophets. Both met God on a mountain (Exodus 24; 1 Kings 19:8-18). Later Jesus shows how the Law and the Prophets speak of his suffering (24:27, 44).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: departure, the exodus
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the plain meaning and keeps the word "exodus", so that the link with Moses can be heard.

decisions.choice: how he would soon leave this world
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what his departure is.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ ἦσαν βεβαρημένοι ὕπνῳ· διαγρηγορήσαντες δὲ εἶδον τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς δύο ἄνδρας τοὺς συνεστῶτας αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And Peter and those with him were heavy with sleep; having awoken fully then they saw the glory of him and the two men standing with him.
pieces: Peter and the others with him had been overcome by sleep. But when they were wide awake, they saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, and the two men who stood beside {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.32: And Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep; but becoming fully awake, they saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory and the two men standing with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.32: Peter and the two others with him had been very sleepy. But then they woke up completely, and they saw the glory of Jesus. They also saw the two men standing with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: becoming fully awake: waking up completely
decisions.reason: The verb can mean either to wake up fully or to keep awake. Since they had been heavy with sleep, waking fits best; but it may mean they struggled and stayed awake, and so saw what happened.

decisions.choice: they saw his glory: the glory that belongs to Jesus himself
decisions.reason: Luke speaks of Jesus' own glory, as in 9:26. Compare John 1:14.

decisions.choice: the two others
decisions.reason: Readable says who was with Peter (9:28).

records.source: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ διαχωρίζεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Ἐπιστάτα, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι, καὶ ποιήσωμεν σκηνὰς τρεῖς, μίαν σοὶ καὶ μίαν Μωϋσεῖ καὶ μίαν Ἠλίᾳ, μὴ εἰδὼς ὃ λέγει.
records.gloss: And it came to pass in the departing of them from him, said Peter to Jesus, Master, good it is for us here to be, also let us make tents three, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah, not knowing what he is saying.
pieces: When the two men were about to part from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, Peter spoke up: "Master, it is good that we are here. We should set up three tents, one for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, one for Moses, one for Elijah." Peter did not really know what he was saying.

L.33: And it happened, as they were parting from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, Peter said to Jesus, "Master, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tents, one for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and one for Moses and one for Elijah," not knowing what he was saying.

R.33: Moses and Elijah were starting to leave Jesus. Then Peter said to Jesus, "Master, it is a good thing that we are here! Let us build three tents. One will be for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." Peter did not understand what he was saying.

decisions.choice: tents: shelters or booths
decisions.reason: The word means a tent or shelter. At the Feast of Booths Israel lived in shelters to remember the wilderness (Leviticus 23:42-43), and God's tent of meeting was where he met Moses. Peter may want to keep the moment from ending.

decisions.choice: as they were parting: Moses and Elijah, as they left
decisions.reason: The two men are about to go; Peter speaks to keep them.

decisions.choice: not knowing what he was saying: Luke's comment
decisions.reason: The narrator explains that Peter's proposal missed the point: Moses and Elijah are not equals of Jesus, as the voice will show (9:35).

decisions.choice: Master: one in charge
decisions.reason: Luke's word for Jesus as the one who gives orders (5:5; 8:24).

decisions.choice: the two men (B); Moses and Elijah (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who was leaving.

records.source: ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ἐγένετο νεφέλη καὶ ἐπεσκίαζεν αὐτούς· ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ ἐν τῷ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν νεφέλην.
records.gloss: These things then as he is saying came a cloud and was overshadowing them; they feared then in the entering of them into the cloud.
pieces: While Peter was still speaking, a cloud came and cast its shadow over them, and they were frightened as they went into the cloud.

L.34: And while he was saying these things, a cloud came and was overshadowing them; and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.

R.34: Peter was still saying this when a cloud came and covered them with its shadow. They became afraid as they went into the cloud.

decisions.choice: a cloud overshadowed them: the cloud of God's presence
decisions.reason: God came down in a cloud on Mount Sinai (Exodus 24:15-18) and filled the tent of meeting with a cloud (Exodus 40:34-35). The same verb is used in 1:35 for the power of the Most High overshadowing Mary.

decisions.choice: as they entered the cloud: who entered is not said
decisions.reason: "Them" and "they" could mean Jesus with Moses and Elijah, or the whole group. The voice comes out of the cloud to the disciples (9:35), and every level keeps the open wording.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

records.source: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἐκλελεγμένος, αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε.
records.gloss: And a voice came out of the cloud saying, This is the Son of me, the one having been chosen, him listen to.
pieces: Then a voice came from the cloud: "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the Chosen One. Listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.35: And a voice came out of the cloud, saying, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the one who has been chosen; listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.35: A voice came from the cloud and said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son. I have chosen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Listen to what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says!"

decisions.choice: chosen: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: beloved, in whom I am well pleased
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts read "the one who has been chosen". Many later manuscripts read "my beloved Son", the wording of Mark 9:7 and of the voice at Jesus' baptism (3:22), and some add "in whom I am well pleased" from Matthew 17:5. The harder and older reading is "chosen". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Chosen One: God's chosen servant
decisions.reason: God speaks of "my chosen one" in whom he delights, the servant who will bring justice (Isaiah 42:1). At the cross the rulers mock Jesus as "the Christ of God, the chosen one" (23:35).

decisions.choice: listen to him: the prophet like Moses
decisions.reason: Moses promised a prophet like himself and said, "Listen to him" (Deuteronomy 18:15). With Moses standing there, the voice points to Jesus.

decisions.choice: a voice: God speaking
decisions.reason: As at the baptism (3:22), the voice is God the Father's, calling Jesus "my Son".

decisions.choice: I have chosen him
decisions.reason: Readable turns the title into a short sentence.

records.source: καὶ ἐν τῷ γενέσθαι τὴν φωνὴν εὑρέθη Ἰησοῦς μόνος.
records.gloss: And as occurred the voice was found Jesus alone.
pieces: When the voice had finished, Jesus was there alone.

L.36: And when the voice had spoken, Jesus was found alone.

R.36: After the voice stopped speaking, the disciples saw that Jesus was alone.

decisions.choice: was found alone: Moses and Elijah were gone
alternatives: Jesus was left without the disciples
decisions.reason: Only Jesus remains, as the voice has said: listen to him.

decisions.choice: the disciples saw
decisions.reason: Readable says who found Jesus alone.

records.source: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐσίγησαν καὶ οὐδενὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις οὐδὲν ὧν ἑώρακαν.
records.gloss: And they were silent and to no one told in those days anything of what they had seen.
pieces: The disciples kept quiet. At that time they said nothing to anyone about the things they had seen.

L.36: And they kept silent and told no one in those days anything of what they had seen.

R.36: The disciples did not say anything about it. At that time they did not tell anyone what they had seen.

decisions.choice: in those days: for that time
decisions.reason: They kept silent then; later Peter spoke of it (2 Peter 1:16-18). Mark 9:9 says Jesus told them to keep it to themselves until he had risen.

decisions.choice: The disciples
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ τῇ ἑξῆς ἡμέρᾳ κατελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄρους συνήντησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς.
records.gloss: It came to pass then the next day having come down of them from the mountain met him a crowd great.
pieces: On the following day, after they had come down the mountain, a big crowd was there to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.37: And it happened on the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a large crowd met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.37: The next day Jesus and the three disciples came down the mountain. A large crowd of people met Jesus there.

decisions.choice: on the next day: they had spent the night on the mountain
decisions.reason: Luke's note implies they stayed on the mountain overnight; Jesus often prayed at night (6:12).

decisions.choice: Jesus and the three disciples
decisions.reason: Readable names who came down.

records.heading: A father's only son is set free

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ἐβόησεν λέγων· Διδάσκαλε, δέομαί σου ἐπιβλέψαι ἐπὶ τὸν υἱόν μου, ὅτι μονογενής μοί ἐστιν, καὶ ἰδοὺ πνεῦμα λαμβάνει αὐτόν, καὶ ἐξαίφνης κράζει, καὶ σπαράσσει αὐτὸν μετὰ ἀφροῦ καὶ μόγις ἀποχωρεῖ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ συντρῖβον αὐτόν·
records.gloss: And behold a man from the crowd cried out saying, Teacher, I implore you to look upon the son of me, for an only child to me he is, \v 39 and behold a spirit takes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it throws into convulsions him with foaming, and scarcely it departs from him, bruising him.
pieces: A man in the crowd shouted, "Teacher, I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, look at my son! He is my only child.
A spirit grabs him, and suddenly he shrieks. It shakes him violently until he foams at the mouth, and it will hardly let him go; it leaves him battered.

L.38: And look, a man from the crowd shouted, saying, "Teacher, I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to look at my son, because he is my only child,
L.39: and look, a spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it convulses him with foaming, and it scarcely goes away from him, bruising him.

R.38: A man in the crowd shouted, "Teacher, please help my son! I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! He is the only child I have.
R.39: A spirit takes control of him, and all at once the boy screams. The spirit shakes him hard, and he foams at the mouth. It almost never leaves him alone, and it is hurting him badly.

decisions.choice: look at: look with care and help
decisions.reason: The verb means to look upon with concern, as God looked upon Mary (1:48).

decisions.choice: he cries out: the boy, or the spirit through him
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. It may be the boy, or the spirit crying out through him, as demons do in 4:33. The other verbs have the spirit as subject.

decisions.choice: scarcely: hardly ever, and only with a struggle
decisions.reason: The word means with difficulty. The spirit rarely leaves the boy, and when it does it leaves him hurt.

decisions.choice: bruising: battering, wearing down
decisions.reason: The verb means to crush or shatter. The fits leave the boy injured and worn out.

decisions.choice: my only child: the father's only son
decisions.reason: Luke notes an only child three times: the widow's son (7:12), Jairus' daughter (8:42) and here. The loss would end the family line.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: please help my son
decisions.reason: Readable says what the father means by asking Jesus to look at his son.

records.source: καὶ ἐδεήθην τῶν μαθητῶν σου ἵνα ἐκβάλωσιν αὐτό, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν.
records.gloss: And I begged the disciples of you that they might cast out it, and not they were able.
pieces: I pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples to drive it out, but they did not have the power."

L.40: And I begged {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples to cast it out, and they were not able."

R.40: I begged {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples to make the spirit leave, but they could not do it."

decisions.choice: they were not able: their failure
decisions.reason: The disciples had been given power over all demons (9:1), yet here they fail. Jesus' answer (9:41) turns to the lack of faith around him.

decisions.choice: make the spirit leave
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what casting out means.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη, ἕως πότε ἔσομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν;
records.gloss: Answering then Jesus said, O generation unbelieving and perverted, until when will I be with you and bear with you?
pieces: Jesus replied, "Oh, this generation, with no faith and so twisted! How long must I be with you and put up with you?

L.41: And Jesus answered and said, "O unbelieving and perverted generation, how long will I be with you and bear with you?

R.41: Jesus answered, "You people of today do not believe God, and you have turned away from what is right! How long must I stay with you and put up with you?

decisions.choice: unbelieving and perverted generation: words used of Israel in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Moses calls Israel a crooked and twisted generation (Deuteronomy 32:5), children without faithfulness (Deuteronomy 32:20).

decisions.choice: generation: the people of this time
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the whole generation, which includes the disciples who failed and the crowd. He does not single anyone out.

decisions.choice: how long will I be with you: a cry of grief
alternatives: a question asking for a date
decisions.reason: The question expresses grief at their unbelief, as God says "How long?" of Israel (Numbers 14:11, 27).

decisions.choice: do not believe God
decisions.reason: Readable turns the adjective into a plain statement. The word is not the key word "faith", so Readable is free to use the verb "believe".

records.source: προσάγαγε ὧδε τὸν υἱόν σου.
records.gloss: Bring here the son of you.
pieces: Bring your son here."

decisions.choice: your son: spoken to the father
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular; Jesus turns from the generation to the father.

decisions.choice: to me
decisions.reason: Readable says where the boy is to come.

records.source: ἔτι δὲ προσερχομένου αὐτοῦ ἔρρηξεν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον καὶ συνεσπάραξεν· ἐπετίμησεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ, καὶ ἰάσατο τὸν παῖδα καὶ ἀπέδωκεν αὐτὸν τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: While then he was coming near, threw down him the demon and threw into convulsions; rebuked then Jesus the spirit the unclean and healed the boy and gave back him to the father of him.
pieces: The boy was still on his way when the demon dashed him to the ground and shook him violently. But Jesus gave the unclean spirit a stern command. He healed the boy and returned him to his father.

L.42: And while he was still coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed [him]; but Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.

R.42: While the boy was coming to Jesus, the demon threw him down and shook him hard. But Jesus spoke sharply to the evil spirit. He healed the boy and gave him back to his father.

decisions.choice: rebuked: commanded with authority
decisions.reason: As in 4:35 and 4:39, Jesus' rebuke is a command that the spirit must obey.

decisions.choice: the demon, the unclean spirit: the same being
decisions.reason: Luke uses both names for it, as in 4:33-35.

decisions.choice: gave him back to his father: as Elijah and Jesus gave back the dead
decisions.reason: Elijah gave the widow's son back to his mother (1 Kings 17:23), and Jesus did the same at Nain (7:15).

decisions.choice: evil spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says "evil spirit", as in Luke 4 and 6. "Unclean" means the spirit makes a person unfit to come near God.

records.source: ἐξεπλήσσοντο δὲ πάντες ἐπὶ τῇ μεγαλειότητι τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Were astonished then all at the majesty of God.
pieces: All the people were astounded at the majesty of God.

L.43: And all were astonished at the majesty of God.

R.43: Everyone was amazed at how great God is.

decisions.choice: majesty: greatness, splendor
decisions.reason: The word is used for God's greatness (2 Peter 1:16, of the transfiguration). The crowd sees God's power at work in Jesus.

records.source: Πάντων δὲ θαυμαζόντων ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐποίει εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: Of all however wondering at all which he was doing, he said to the disciples of him,
pieces: People were still wondering at everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples,

L.43: But while all were marveling at all the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples,

R.43: Everyone was amazed at all the things Jesus was doing. But Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples,

decisions.choice: while all were marveling: Jesus speaks against the mood of the crowd
decisions.reason: In the middle of the crowd's wonder Jesus tells his disciples of his betrayal.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

records.heading: Jesus speaks again of being handed over

records.source: Θέσθε ὑμεῖς εἰς τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ὁ γὰρ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: Let sink you into the ears of you the words these, for the Son of Man is about to be betrayed into [the] hands of men.
pieces: "Let these words sink deep into your ears: the Son of Man is going to be handed over into the hands of {{gender:human beings|men}}."

L.44: "Put these words into your ears, for the Son of Man is about to be handed over into [the] hands of {{gender:people|men}}."

R.44: "Remember well what I am telling you. Soon the Son of Man will be handed over to the power of {{gender:people|men}}."

decisions.choice: put these words into your ears: listen and hold on to this
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of saying pay close attention and remember (Exodus 17:14).

decisions.choice: handed over: given into the power of others
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over. It is used for Judas' betrayal (22:4) and for the council handing Jesus to Pilate (24:20); behind both, God gives up his Son (Romans 8:32).

decisions.choice: men: human beings
decisions.reason: The word means people in general. The Son of Man is handed over to human beings.

decisions.choice: into the hands of: into the power of
decisions.reason: A common Hebrew way of speaking of power over someone (Genesis 9:2).

decisions.choice: Remember well what I am telling you.
alternatives: Let these words sink into your ears
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο, καὶ ἦν παρακεκαλυμμένον ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἵνα μὴ αἴσθωνται αὐτό, καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο ἐρωτῆσαι αὐτὸν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος τούτου.
records.gloss: But they understand not the saying this, and it was veiled from them that not they should understand it, and they were afraid to ask him concerning the saying this.
pieces: They did not know what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant by this. It had been veiled from them so that they would not see what it meant. And they were afraid to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said.

L.45: But they did not understand this saying, and it was concealed from them, so that they would not perceive it; and they were afraid to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about this saying.

R.45: But the disciples did not know what these words meant. Their meaning was kept hidden from them, so they could not understand. They were also afraid to ask Jesus to explain it.

decisions.choice: it was concealed from them: God kept its meaning hidden for a time
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the one who hid it unnamed. In 24:45 Jesus opens their minds to understand the Scriptures, which shows the hiding was for a time.

decisions.choice: so that they would not perceive it: the purpose or the result
alternatives: only a result: as a result they did not perceive it
decisions.reason: The construction usually gives a purpose, but can give a result. The levels keep "so that", which allows both.

decisions.choice: saying: a spoken statement
decisions.reason: The word means a thing said; it refers to the words of 9:44.

decisions.choice: to explain it
decisions.reason: Readable says what they were afraid to ask.

records.source: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ διαλογισμὸς ἐν αὐτοῖς, τὸ τίς ἂν εἴη μείζων αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: Came up then an argument among them, this who might be greatest of them.
pieces: A dispute came up among them: which of them was the greatest?

L.46: And an argument arose among them, as to which of them might be the greatest.

R.46: The disciples began to argue about which one of them was the most important.

decisions.choice: argument: a dispute, a debate of thoughts
decisions.reason: The word means reasoning or debate; 9:47 uses it of the thoughts in their hearts.

decisions.choice: greatest: the comparative form used as the highest
decisions.reason: The Greek has the form "greater", but with "of them" it means the greatest of the group, as often in New Testament Greek.

decisions.choice: the most important
decisions.reason: Readable says what greatness means here: rank and importance.

records.heading: Who is the greatest

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἰδὼς τὸν διαλογισμὸν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενος παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ παρ’ ἑαυτῷ, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὃς ἂν δέξηται τοῦτο τὸ παιδίον ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐμὲ δέξηται δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με· ὁ γὰρ μικρότερος ἐν πᾶσιν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχων οὗτός ἐστιν μέγας.
records.gloss: But Jesus having known the reasoning of the heart of them having taken hold of a child set it by himself, \v 48 and he said to them, Whoever shall receive this child in the name of me me receives, and whoever me shall receive receives the [one] having sent me; the [one] for least among all you being, he shall be great.
pieces: Jesus knew what they were thinking in their hearts. He took a child and had the child stand beside {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Anyone who receives this child in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is receiving {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And anyone who receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is receiving the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. For whoever is least among all of you, that is the one who is great."

L.47: But Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their heart, took hold of a child [and] stood it beside {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}},
L.48: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Whoever receives this child in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; and whoever receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} receives the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. For the one who is least among you all, this one is great."

R.47: Jesus knew what they were thinking. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took a little child and stood the child next to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.48: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "When someone welcomes this little child because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that person is welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And when someone welcomes {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that person is welcoming God, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. The one who is least important among all of you is the one who is great."

decisions.choice: receive: welcome as a guest
decisions.reason: The verb is used for welcoming someone into one's home (9:5, 53). A child had no standing; to welcome one for Jesus' sake is to welcome Jesus.

decisions.choice: in my name: for my sake, as belonging to me
decisions.reason: To do something in someone's name is to do it on their behalf and because of them.

decisions.choice: the one who sent me: God
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of being sent by God (4:18, 43).

decisions.choice: is great: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "is great". Many manuscripts have "will be great". The difference is small: greatness belongs to the least, now or at the end. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a child: a small child, someone with no rank
decisions.reason: Children had no power or status in the ancient world.

decisions.choice: God, who sent me
decisions.reason: Readable names the sender.

decisions.choice: because of me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

records.source: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Ἰωάννης εἶπεν· Ἐπιστάτα, εἴδομέν τινα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια, καὶ ἐκωλύομεν αὐτὸν ὅτι οὐκ ἀκολουθεῖ μεθ’ ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: Answering then John said, Master, we saw someone in the name of you casting out demons, and we were forbidding him because not he follows with us.
pieces: John responded, "Master, we saw a man driving out demons by using {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and we kept telling him to stop, because he is not a follower along with us."

L.49: And John answered and said, "Master, we saw someone casting out demons in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not follow with us."

R.49: John said, "Master, we saw a man forcing demons out of people by using {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. We told him to stop, because he is not part of our group."

decisions.choice: we tried to stop him: kept forbidding
alternatives: stopped him once and for all
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes repeated or attempted action.

decisions.choice: in your name: calling on Jesus' name with his authority
decisions.reason: The man used Jesus' name to command the demons, and it worked. Compare Acts 19:13-16, where men who did not know Jesus tried it and failed.

decisions.choice: he does not follow with us: he is not one of our company
alternatives: he does not follow Jesus at all
decisions.reason: John's complaint is that the man is not part of the Twelve's group.

decisions.choice: John answered: a reply to Jesus' words about the least
decisions.reason: John's question comes straight after the saying on greatness and receiving in Jesus' name.

records.heading: Not against you, but for you

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ κωλύετε, ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθ’ ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐστιν.
records.gloss: Said then to him Jesus, Not forbid, whoever for not is against you for you is.
pieces: Jesus told him, "Do not try to stop him. Anyone who is not against you is on your side."

L.50: But Jesus said to him, "Do not forbid [him]; for whoever is not against you is for you."

R.50: Jesus said to John, "Do not stop him. Anyone who is not against you is helping you."

decisions.choice: you: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "against us ... for us". The earliest have "you", meaning the disciples. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: whoever is not against you is for you: a generous rule
decisions.reason: In 11:23 Jesus says that whoever is not with him is against him. That saying is about those who oppose him; this one is about those who serve in his name.

decisions.choice: on your side (B); helping you (R)
decisions.reason: Plain English for being on someone's side.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ἀναλήμψεως αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς τὸ πρόσωπον ἐστήρισεν τοῦ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ ἀπέστειλεν ἀγγέλους πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: It came to pass then in the completing the days of the taking up of him that he the face steadfastly set to go to Jerusalem, \v 52 and he sent messengers before [the] face of him.
pieces: As the time drew near for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be taken up, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face toward Jerusalem, determined to go there.
He sent messengers on ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.51: Now it happened, when the days of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} being taken up were being fulfilled, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] face to go to Jerusalem,

R.51: The time was coming near when God would take Jesus up to heaven. So Jesus firmly decided to go to Jerusalem.
R.52: He sent some messengers ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: being taken up: his going up to God
alternatives: his being lifted onto the cross
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb used for Jesus' ascension (Acts 1:2, 11, 22) and for Elijah's being taken up (2 Kings 2:9-11). It looks ahead to all that happens in Jerusalem: his death, resurrection and ascension.

decisions.choice: set his face: made up his mind firmly
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of speaking of firm purpose (Isaiah 50:7; Ezekiel 21:2). From here Luke tells the story as one long journey to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: when the days were being fulfilled: as the time came near
alternatives: when the time had already passed
decisions.reason: The present tense describes days moving toward their completion. Luke uses the same word for the time of Pentecost (Acts 2:1).

decisions.choice: before his face: ahead of him
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of saying in front of, as in 7:27. Luke repeats "face" in 9:51, 52 and 53.

decisions.choice: turned his face toward Jerusalem, determined to go there
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the face and says what it means.

decisions.choice: when God would take Jesus up to heaven
decisions.reason: Readable says who takes him up and where.

records.heading: A Samaritan village turns Jesus away

records.source: καὶ πορευθέντες εἰσῆλθον εἰς κώμην Σαμαριτῶν, ὡς ἑτοιμάσαι αὐτῷ·
records.gloss: And having gone they entered into a village of the Samaritans so as to make ready for him.
pieces: On their way they went into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.52: And going, they entered into a village of Samaritans, so as to make ready for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.52: They went into a town where Samaritans lived. They wanted to get things ready for Jesus to stay there.

decisions.choice: Samaritans: the people of Samaria, between Galilee and Judea
decisions.reason: The Samaritans worshiped the God of Israel but held that the place of worship was Mount Gerizim, not Jerusalem (John 4:20). Jews and Samaritans were hostile to each other (John 4:9).

decisions.choice: so as to make ready: to arrange food and lodging
alternatives: to prepare the people to hear him
decisions.reason: The messengers go ahead to prepare for Jesus and his company to stay.

decisions.choice: for Jesus to stay there
decisions.reason: Readable says what was being made ready.

records.source: καὶ οὐκ ἐδέξαντο αὐτόν, ὅτι τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἦν πορευόμενον εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.
records.gloss: And not they did receive him, because the face of him was going toward Jerusalem.
pieces: But the people there refused to welcome {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, since {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face was turned toward Jerusalem.

L.53: And they did not receive {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face was going toward Jerusalem.

R.53: But the people of that town would not welcome Jesus, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: because he was going to Jerusalem: the dispute over the place of worship
alternatives: because they did not know him
decisions.reason: Pilgrims passing through Samaria on the way to the feasts in Jerusalem were not welcome, since Samaritans rejected Jerusalem as the place to worship (John 4:20).

decisions.choice: his face was going: he was heading
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew way of speaking as 9:51.

decisions.choice: he was on his way
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

records.source: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης εἶπαν· Κύριε, θέλεις εἴπωμεν πῦρ καταβῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀναλῶσαι αὐτούς;
records.gloss: Having seen [it] now the disciples James and John said, Lord, will you [that] we should call fire to come down from heaven and to consume them?
pieces: Seeing this, the disciples James and John said, "Lord, is it {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wish that we command fire to come down from heaven and burn them up?"

L.54: And seeing [this], the disciples James and John said, "Lord, do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to call fire to come down from heaven and consume them?"
