R.54: James and John saw what happened. They said, "Lord, do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to tell fire to come down from heaven and burn up these people?"

decisions.choice: fire to come down from heaven: as in the days of Elijah
decisions.reason: Elijah called down fire from heaven on soldiers sent by the king of Samaria (2 Kings 1:10-12). James and John want to do the same to a Samaritan village.

decisions.choice: consume them: the reading of the SBLGNT, without "as Elijah also did"
alternatives: consume them, as Elijah also did
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "as Elijah also did". The earliest manuscripts lack it, and it looks like a note that spelled out the allusion. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Lord: master, and more
decisions.reason: The disciples address Jesus with respect, using the word that also stands for God.

decisions.choice: these people
decisions.reason: Readable names whom the fire would burn.

records.source: στραφεὶς δὲ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: Having turned then he rebuked them.
pieces: But Jesus turned and gave them a stern rebuke.

R.55: But Jesus turned and told them firmly that they were wrong.

decisions.choice: he rebuked them: the reading of the SBLGNT, with nothing added
alternatives: he rebuked them and said, You do not know what kind of spirit you are of, for the Son of Man did not come to destroy people's lives but to save them
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add, "and he said, 'You do not know what kind of spirit you are of'", and some go on, "for the Son of Man did not come to destroy people's lives but to save them" (compare 19:10). The earliest manuscripts have none of these words, which were probably added to say what the rebuke was. The SBLGNT leaves them out. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he rebuked them: Jesus refuses to punish the village
decisions.reason: "Them" is James and John. Jesus' way to Jerusalem is not one of vengeance (compare 6:27-29).

decisions.choice: told them firmly that they were wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what a rebuke is.

records.source: καὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς ἑτέραν κώμην.
records.gloss: And they went to another village.
pieces: And they went on to a different village.

L.56: And they went to another village.

R.56: Then they all went to another village.

decisions.choice: the verse as in the SBLGNT, without the longer words before it
alternatives: for the Son of Man did not come to destroy people's lives but to save them; and they went to another village
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts place the added saying (see 9:55) at the start of this verse. The SBLGNT does not include it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: another village: perhaps another Samaritan village
decisions.reason: Luke does not say whether it was Samaritan.

records.source: Καὶ πορευομένων αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπέν τις πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀκολουθήσω σοι ὅπου ἐὰν ἀπέρχῃ.
records.gloss: And going of them on the road said someone to him, I will follow you wherever you may go.
pieces: While they were going along the road, someone told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Wherever {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go, I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.57: And as they were going along the road, someone said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wherever {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go."

R.57: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were walking along the road. Someone said to Jesus, "I will go with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} anywhere {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go."

decisions.choice: follow: go with as a disciple
decisions.reason: To follow Jesus is to become his disciple (5:11, 27-28; 9:23).

decisions.choice: going on the road: on the journey to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The road is the journey that began in 9:51. The three would-be followers meet Jesus on his way to his death.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who was on the road.

records.heading: Would-be followers on the road

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Αἱ ἀλώπεκες φωλεοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνώσεις, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνῃ.
records.gloss: And said to him Jesus, The foxes holes have and the birds of the air nests, but the Son of Man not has where the head he might lay.
pieces: Jesus said to him, "Foxes have their holes, and the birds in the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay down {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head."

L.58: And Jesus said to him, "The foxes have holes and the birds of the sky [have] nests, but the Son of Man does not have [a place] where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may lay [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] head."

R.58: Jesus answered him, "Foxes have holes to live in, and birds have nests. But the Son of Man does not even have a home where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can lay down {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head to rest."

decisions.choice: nowhere to lay his head: no home of his own
decisions.reason: Jesus has left home for the road and lives on what others give (8:3). Whoever follows him must be ready to live the same way.

decisions.choice: the birds of the sky: wild birds
decisions.reason: The word for "sky" is the same as "heaven"; the phrase means wild birds.

decisions.choice: a home ... to rest
decisions.reason: Readable says what the saying means.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς ἕτερον· Ἀκολούθει μοι.
records.gloss: He said then to another, Follow me.
pieces: To another man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.59: Jesus said to another man, "Come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: another: another man
decisions.reason: The word is masculine, and in 9:59 he speaks of his father.

decisions.choice: follow me: become my disciple
decisions.reason: The same call that Levi answered (5:27-28).

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ἀπελθόντι πρῶτον θάψαι τὸν πατέρα μου.
records.gloss: But he said, Lord, allow me having gone away first to bury the father of me.
pieces: But the man replied, "Lord, allow me to go first and bury my father."

L.59: But he said, "Lord, allow me first to go away [and] bury my father."

R.59: But the man said, "Lord, let me first go and bury my father."

decisions.choice: Lord: the reading of the SBLGNT, printed in brackets there
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "Lord"; others have it. The SBLGNT prints it in brackets to show doubt. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: bury my father: a son's most sacred duty
decisions.reason: Burying one's parents came before almost every other duty in Jewish life. The father may have just died, or the son may mean that he will follow once his father has died, which could be years away.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς, σὺ δὲ ἀπελθὼν διάγγελλε τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: He said then to him, Leave the dead to bury the their own dead, you however having gone forth declare the kingdom of God.
pieces: Jesus told him, "Leave the dead to bury their own dead. As for you, go and spread the news of the kingdom of God everywhere."

L.60: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Let the dead bury their own dead, but you, go away and proclaim the kingdom of God."

R.60: Jesus answered, "Leave the dead to bury their own dead. You must go and tell people everywhere about the kingdom of God."

decisions.choice: let the dead bury their own dead: a deliberately shocking saying
decisions.reason: The first "dead" probably means those who do not have the life of God's kingdom; they can see to the dead body. The saying shows how urgent the call to the kingdom is.

decisions.choice: proclaim: spread the news far and wide
decisions.reason: The verb means to announce everywhere.

decisions.choice: but you: emphatic, set against the dead
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands out: his task is different from theirs.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ καὶ ἕτερος· Ἀκολουθήσω σοι, κύριε· πρῶτον δὲ ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ἀποτάξασθαι τοῖς εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου.
records.gloss: Said then also another, I will follow you, Lord; first however allow me to bid farewell to those at the home of me.
pieces: Yet another said, "I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord, but allow me first to take leave of the people at my home."

L.61: And another also said, "I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord; but first allow me to say farewell to those at my home."

R.61: Then someone else said, "Lord, I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. But first I want to go and say goodbye to the people in my house."

decisions.choice: first let me say farewell: like Elisha's request
decisions.reason: When Elijah called Elisha from the plow, Elisha asked to kiss his father and mother goodbye, and Elijah let him (1 Kings 19:19-21). Jesus' call is more urgent than Elijah's.

decisions.choice: those at my home: the people of my household
decisions.reason: The form could mean people or things; with "say farewell" it means people.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδεὶς ἐπιβαλὼν τὴν χεῖρα ἐπ’ ἄροτρον καὶ βλέπων εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω εὔθετός ἐστιν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Said then Jesus, No one having laid the hand upon [the] plow and looking at the things behind fit is for the kingdom of God.
pieces: Jesus answered, "No one who sets a hand to the plow and keeps looking back is suited for the kingdom of God."

L.62: But Jesus said, "No one who has put the hand on a plow and is looking at the things behind is fit for the kingdom of God."

R.62: Jesus said, "Anyone who starts to plow a field and then keeps looking back is no use for the kingdom of God."

decisions.choice: a hand on the plow, looking back: a plowman who cannot cut a straight furrow
decisions.reason: A man plowing with oxen had to keep his eyes ahead to keep the furrow straight. The picture recalls Elisha, who was plowing when he was called (1 Kings 19:19).

decisions.choice: looking: keeps looking
decisions.reason: The present participle describes looking back again and again.

decisions.choice: fit: suitable, well suited
decisions.reason: The word means useful or suited for a task. Such a person is of no use for the work of the kingdom.

decisions.choice: is no use
decisions.reason: Readable puts the point plainly.
